title: Autonomous SLI Autotune and Operator Validation Loop
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This runbook defines the autonomous SLI autotune pipeline used to adjust SLI thresholds for runtime inference services and the operator validation loop that must run after any automated changes. It combines metric-driven tuning, canary validation, and a short manual/automated review window to avoid regression of customer-facing SLOs while reducing alert noise and manual adjustments.

Purpose and goals:
- Reduce manual SLI threshold churn by up to 60% for noisy signals.
- Ensure autotuned thresholds do not cause SLO regressions or inappropriate mitigations (evictions, throttles).
- Provide clear operator steps and escalation for any autotune misbehavior.

Scope:
- Applies to token-latency, token-cost, model-quality (regression score), and request-success rate SLIs for services: runtime-inference, batch-embeddings, and routing-gateway.
- Not for: billing integrity SLIs, security/auth SLIs, or customer-reported correctness incidents.

Quick summary of flow:
1) Telemetry window and candidate generation (automated).
2) Candidate simulation against historical workload (automated).
3) Canary rollout of new thresholds to 2% traffic (automated).
4) Operator validation window (3–6 hours) with well-defined checks (semi-automated/manual).
5) Promote or rollback (automated with safety checks or manual).

When to run this runbook:
- The autotune pipeline has flagged a candidate threshold change (alerts: AUTOTUNE_CANDIDATE_READY).
- Post-incident when metric distributions shifted and we need safe re-baselining.
- Quarterly SLI hygiene if no changes occurred automatically.

Prerequisites and ownership:
- Ownership: Observability team (primary), Runtime SRE (secondary).
- Required dashboards: SLI Autotune Overview, Canary Verdict Panel, Regression Detector (see Monitoring section).
- Credentials: operator role in redwoodctl with scope: observability:write and runtime:canary-deploy.

Key service names and components referenced:
- telemetry-ingest (metric collection)
- sli-autotuner (autotune pipeline service)
- canary-router (traffic gating service)
- runtime-inference (primary target service)
- redwoodctl (CLI for orchestration)

Steady-state configuration table (defaults):
| parameter | default | rationale | operator action if violated |
|---|---:|---|---|
| analysis_window | 6h | balance recentness vs noise | increase to 24h if insufficient data |
| candidate_confidence | 0.90 | require robust statistical signal | lower to 0.85 for low-volume services with reviewer approval |
| canary_fraction | 0.02 | small blast radius | do not exceed 0.05 without PM approval |
| validation_window | 4h | typical workload cycle coverage | extend to 12h for weekly-batched spikes |
| rollback_threshold_delta | 10% | rollback if SLI moves >10% worse | immediate rollback and incident bridge |

Candidate generation and simulation (automated):
1) sli-autotuner pulls metric series for the analysis_window and computes candidate thresholds (percentiles, Holt-Winters adjusted bounds).
2) It then simulates the candidate by replaying a sampled historical request set through the "virtual SLO fence" to estimate impact on SLO burn, token-cost, and alert counts.
3) If simulation passes heuristics (no predicted SLO burn > 5% and alert reduction > 15%), candidate is promoted to canary stage and AUTOTUNE_CANDIDATE_READY alert is emitted to #observability-autotune.

Commands and snippets (useful for on-call operators):
- Check candidate details:
```
redwoodctl autotune describe --id <candidate-id>
```
- Simulate locally (developer machine with sample trace):
```
redwoodctl autotune simulate --id <candidate-id> --trace samples/2026-02-13-peak.json
```
- Manually trigger canary rollout:
```
redwoodctl canary deploy --service runtime-inference --slis token_latency_p95=180ms --fraction 0.02 --ref <candidate-id>
```

Canary validation checks (operator validation loop):
- Automated checks (must pass for no manual intervention):
  - Canary token-latency p95 change <= rollback_threshold_delta relative to baseline.
  - Request success rate drop < 0.1%.
  - No increase in model-quality regression alerts above noise floor.
  - Error budgets across dependent services unchanged or improved.
- Operator manual checks (perform during validation_window):
  1) Inspect Canary Verdict Panel (dash: canary/verdict) for unstated anomalies.
  2) Run sample end-to-end request set against canary path and confirm outputs consistent with baseline (use quality-checker CLI below).
  3) Confirm cost signal patterns in TokenCostExplainer show expected reduction or acceptable delta.

Manual quality-checker CLI:
```
redwoodctl qual-check --canary-ref <candidate-id> --workload samples/e2e-demo.json --accept-threshold 0.98
```
Report is created in /tmp/qual-report-<candidate-id>.json — upload to the incident channel if any metric < accept-threshold.

Decision matrix after validation_window (promote / hold / rollback):
- Promote automatically if: all automated checks pass AND no manual objection in #observability-autotune for the validation_window.
- Hold if: marginal failures (one automated check failed with delta within 2x rollback_threshold_delta) — requires manual sign-off from runtime SRE.
- Rollback if: any automated check fails beyond rollback_threshold_delta or manual objection citing customer impact.

Automated rollback steps (triggered by canary-verdict engine):
1) canary-router drains new threshold route and re-injects original thresholds.
2) Autotuner records failure reason and increases candidate_confidence requirement for subsequent runs.
3) Incident bridge is opened if rollback was triggered by SLO regression (severity rule: SLO_burn_increase > 5%).

Escalation and communication:
- If rollback due to SLO regression: open incident bridge (PagerDuty: Observability SLO) and notify product owners for any customer-impacting models.
- If repeated autotune failures for same service (>3 within 7 days): schedule a retro with Observability + Runtime SRE + Product to review metric definitions and detection heuristics.

Safety nets and throttles:
- Leaky-bucket backing: canary-router enforces per-service canary qps caps during rollout.
- Operator mute window: if the operator mutes alerts for the service during validation_window, autotune will pause and require manual resume.

Monitoring and dashboards (minimum required panels):
- SLI Autotune Overview: list of active candidates, status, predicted impact, owner, last-run timestamp.
- Canary Verdict Panel: real-time p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost deltas for canary vs baseline.
- Regression Detector: anomaly detector for model-quality score drift (F1, rouge, embed-sim).
- Autotune Audit Trail: event log with candidate-id, decisions, operator signatures.

Alerting contract (examples):
- AUTOTUNE_CANDIDATE_READY: level=info, channel=#observability-autotune, owner=Observability.
- AUTOTUNE_CANARY_FAIL: level=critical, page=Observability SLO rotation, runbook=this doc.
- CANARY_MANUAL_OBJECTION: level=warning, channel=#observability-autotune, owner=runtime-sre.

Runbook: step-by-step operator validation (emergency condensed):
1) Respond to AUTOTUNE_CANDIDATE_READY: `redwoodctl autotune describe --id <candidate-id>` and open a temporary thread in #observability-autotune with candidate details.
2) If candidate simulation indicates low risk, trigger canary (command above).
3) Monitor Canary Verdict Panel for first 30 minutes; check p95, error rate, and model-quality quick sample.
4) If obvious regression observed: run `redwoodctl canary rollback --ref <candidate-id>` and open bridge.
5) If stable after first 30 min, continue a full validation_window of 4h and run full qual-check at hour 1 and hour 3.
6) At the end of validation_window, if no objections and automated checks green, promote with `redwoodctl autotune promote --id <candidate-id>`.

Post-promotion tasks:
- Autotuner writes change record to Autotune Audit Trail and tags release with operator id.
- Observability team schedules a 7-day quick look: automated script will snapshot SLI burn and token-cost over 7 days; if unexpected regressions appear, initiate a regression triage.

Retrospective triggers (automatic):
- Any rollback that required manual rollback + bridge.
- Three or more holds for the same service in a 14-day window.
- Significant divergence between predicted and observed cost savings (>30%).

Retro checklist (if triggered):
- Collect candidate traces, simulation vs observed delta, and operator decision notes.
- Re-evaluate metric definitions with Product/Research on model-quality metrics.
- Decide whether to increase analysis_window or adjust confidence thresholds.

Audit and compliance notes:
- All autotune decisions, canary deploys, operator approvals, and rollbacks are recorded centrally in Autotune Audit Trail and retained for 2 years.
- For customer-sensitive models (label: customer-sensitive), autotune is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by a privacy review.

Appendix: troubleshooting common failure modes:
- Failure: Canary p95 spikes immediately after promotion.
  - Likely cause: workload mismatch between simulation trace and live traffic.
  - Action: rollback, attach trace, increase simulation sample diversity, and rerun.
- Failure: Qual-check reports semantic regression while metrics look fine.
  - Likely cause: quality metric blindspot or distribution shift.
  - Action: open model-quality retro with Research, pause autotune for that model family.
- Failure: Autotune generates candidates too frequently for a low-volume service.
  - Likely cause: confidence threshold too low.
  - Action: increase candidate_confidence for low-volume tag, or exclude service from autotune.
